newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi dlr jumps 20 bp on RBNZ comment, bills yawn.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi dlr jumps 20 bp on RBNZ comment, bills yawn.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar spiked about 20 basis points higher but bill rates barely moved after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand on Monday said monetary conditions were too loose.

The kiwi jumped to US$0.6440 from around US$0.6420 when Reserve Bank chief financial manager David Archer issued a statement at 0100 GMT saying conditions had eased too far from the bank's desired levels.
"Overall monetary conditions have become too loose, given our currenct monetary policy stance" Archer said.

The rise in the currency reined in the Monetary Conditions Index to 102 basis points easier than the RBNZ's desired level of 825 in the September quarter. The MCI had been about 125 points easier prior to the statement.
The money market took a laid back approach to the RB's comments, leaving most of the tightening work to be done by the currency.

Although the 90-day bank yields rose three basis points to 8.27 percent, there remained a bid tone to the market. At 1.25 p.m. (0125 GMT) the MCI was back down to 111 basis points easier than the RB's desired level.
"There wasn't a huge reaction," one bill dealer said.
Asked what the bank was attempting to do, the dealer said: "They are drawing a line in the sand. There had to be some point the bank defended."
The market last week was pushing the MCI around five basis points easier a day, testing the bank's tolerance levels.
